Although substitutes can be found for many metals and minerals currently in use it has become clear that the burning of fossil fuels will have to stop even before geologic resources are depleted because of climatic changes resulting from carbon dioxide concentrations.  Energy can be expected to be in short supply after the disappearance of fossil fuels and the smaller the world population the higher the per capita energy consumption that will be available.  Food supply is a resource that cannot be expanded indefinitely and for which there is no substitute.  Industrial countries have been able to support a population per unit of agricultural area much higher that that which agrarian countries can support at the same standard or have become dependent on external trade for their food supply. Industrialization has emerged as the sole means by which populous agrarian developing countries can eradicate poverty.  A massive transfer of the rural population to urban areas or the successful development of rural industri es is required for farm sizes and farmers incomes to approach those in developed countries.  Conversely industrialization is no guarantee of continued economic growth.  Avoidance of vulnerability to shifts in international economic competition would require each country to be self-sufficient which would be feasible only in a world with a small population.
